hook_text: Right now, while you watch this, Africa is moving. About as fast as your fingernails grow.
clip_script: The ground feels solid, but the Earth's crust is cracked into giant pieces called tectonic plates, and they never stop moving. Underneath them is the mantle, thousands of kilometres of rock so hot it flows like super-thick toffee. Heat rises, cools and sinks, and the plates ride along on top, a few centimetres a year. A hundred years ago, a scientist named Alfred Wegener noticed that Africa and South America fit together like jigsaw pieces, with the same fossils on both sides. Once, all the continents were one giant land called Pangaea. Where plates pull apart, new crust is born. Where they crash, mountains rise and volcanoes erupt. And somewhere, deep in the middle, is a solid iron ball as hot as the surface of the sun.
visual_style: A whiteboard Earth cut open like a peach showing crust, mantle and core; arrows of convection loops; Africa and South America sliding together into a jigsaw fit; a mountain crumpling up.
pacing: Personal hook, a journey to the core, a jigsaw reveal.
